core.description: Envelope-I/O baseline for every action: cat, jq, the mcp__outpost__ submit tools, ToolSearch. Implicit for every runner:claude action. The cat/jq rules name the verb only — which FILE they may open is decided structurally by readArgsAllowed (allowlist.ts), which confines them to $OUTPOST_ENVELOPE, the session's own worktree, and any granted Read: path. That bar is skipped entirely for an action holding a whole-tool Read grant (i.e. anything inheriting `read`), so it binds exactly the actions that never asked to read files. Grants no network access — an action that POSTs back to the daemon carries its own anchored curl rule in its allowlist.json.

read.description: Local file reads and git-read-only commands (Read/Glob/Grep/LS, ls/cat/rg/find, git status/log/diff/show/blame/branch/fetch, sed restricted to a line-range print).

pull.description: Network reads: WebFetch/WebSearch, read-only MCP calls (get_/list_/search_ patterns) against Linear/Datadog/GitHub/Notion/Slack/incident-io/Grafana, curl -s, and read-only gh commands.
alwaysAllowBashPatterns: ^gh (pr view|pr list|pr checks|pr diff|pr status|run view|run list|run watch|workflow view|workflow list|repo view|issue view|issue list|search|release view|release list|label list|cache list|browse)(\s|$)

edit.description: Local writes and test runners: Edit/Write/MultiEdit scoped to /tmp/, npm/yarn/pnpm/go/pytest/cargo/turbo, mage limited to its two evidenced targets, npx limited to the one evidenced typecheck invocation, docker limited to a status check, local git as an anchored whitelist (git rebase <ref> with no --exec/-x, git checkout -- <path>, git merge <ref>/--abort, git add -A/<path> — no -C <path> prefix, no stash/reset/restore/cherry-pick/revert/clean/switch/apply/mv/rm; none evidenced by any edit-inheriting SKILL.md, see permission-group-edit-ceiling.test.ts). node/tsx/vitest/jest/playwright/eslint/prettier/make dropped as bare grants — none had evidenced direct use, and a bare npx/make can't be anchored safely (the danger is in the target, not the command line); see permission-group-edit.test.ts.

push.description: External writes. Every call here is gated: it runs only when pinned by a write draft the user approved, so these rules name the WRITE and let the approval card show the payload, rather than enumerating every permissible flag. Rules must match writes ONLY — matching a read (bare `git tag`, a GET `gh api`) would demand a draft before an action could read. Two structural bars are enforced in code rather than spelled into each rule: --input/--body-file/--notes-file must point under /tmp so the card can render the body being sent (allowlist.ts fileFlagsAllowed), and a force-push, `--mirror`, or `gh pr merge --admin` is refused outright, pin or no pin (dangerous-writes.ts). Everything else dangerous — merging, deleting a ref, a foreign --repo, a raw API write, a URL remote, pushing to a default branch — is surfaced as a warning on the draft instead of being unreachable.
